rationale: C03 is a highly plausible immediate drafting template. Issued only eighteen days earlier, it uses the same extended opening recital identifying the 1947 GATT agreement and Proclamation No. 2761A, the same statutory recital that section 350(a) authorizes partial termination, and the same operative device: terminating the 1947 proclamation to the extent that it thereafter applies as though specified provisions of Schedule XX were altered. The child adapts that concrete structure from concessions associated with China's withdrawal to a fur-felt-hat safeguard action. C08 independently supplies the investigation, hearing, findings, recommendation, and public-interest sequence expressly invoked by the child, while C12 is another close but less exact example of partial termination under the same proclamation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the said proclamation of December 16, 1947, is hereby terminated in part to the extent that, on and after December 1, 1950, it shall be applied as though item 1526(a) in Part I of Schedule XX... were stated as follows
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The said proclamation of December 16, 1947... [is] hereby terminated to the extent that, on and after the sixtieth day following the date of this proclamation [it] shall be applied as though the items and parts of items... were deleted from Part I of Schedule XX... and as though the proviso to Item 760... were stated as follows
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same substantive legal machinery: partial termination of Proclamation No. 2761A implemented by directing that Schedule XX thereafter be applied as though specified tariff text had been deleted or restated.
